title: Flat finite-presentation maps with dense irreducible fibres have irreducible source
statement: Let $R\to T$ be a ring map. Assume that $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is irreducible [def-weil-irreducible-components], that $R\to T$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] and of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and that the fibre rings $T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] have irreducible spectra for a dense set of primes $\mathfrak p$ of $R$. Then $\operatorname{Spec}(T)$ is irreducible.

proof.text: By flatness and finite presentation, the induced map $\operatorname{Spec}(T)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is open, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-finite-presentation-open].

source.place: Algebra, Proposition 00I1 (proposition-fppf-open), as invoked in the proof of Lemma 00I6

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-irreducible-on-top] to this open map $f:\operatorname{Spec}(T)\to\operatorname{Spec}(R)$: the target $\operatorname{Spec}(R)$ is irreducible by hypothesis, and for each prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R$ the fibre $f^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$, with the subspace topology, is homeomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}(T\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ by [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-spec-homeomorphism]; irreducibility is preserved by homeomorphisms, so $f^{-1}(\mathfrak p)$ is irreducible for every $\mathfrak p$ in the given dense set of primes. The conclusion is that $\operatorname{Spec}(T)$ is irreducible.
